claims.statement: The Electricity Directive provides for market-based procurement of flexibility services from distributed generation, demand response and energy storage.
EU electricity-market rules contemplate aggregation and non-discriminatory market access for demand response and storage.

contrary_evidence: EU market principles do not establish Polish product eligibility, accessible revenue pools or viable economics for small sites.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: embed opt-in and compatible controls in battery, HVAC and refrigeration installer handover.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: control 2 MW in year 2, 15 MW by year 4, build 4 million PLN founder equity and cash by year 6, and reach 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 7-10.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day after monitoring and incident response are staffed.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 45%-70% gross margin after gateway, telemetry, partner and support costs at sufficient device density.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 18-36 months, depending on market qualification, device density and revenue per controllable kilowatt.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: retain 15%-30% of net flexibility revenue after the site and licensed market partner are paid.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: contracts could renew annually because installed devices persist, but churn and opt-out are unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Every activation improves the private response and reliability model, enabling tighter bids and better site selection
fingerprint.customer: SMEs with controllable energy assets and licensed flexibility-market participants needing aggregated capacity
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Opt-in contracts and controls embedded in installer commissioning
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed device aggregation without initially becoming the licensed market participant
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A licensed partner or market counterparty pays for availability or activation; proceeds are shared
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A compatible asset is installed but earns no grid-service revenue

founder_fit: Combines energy access with predictive modelling.
Can start through a licensed partner rather than a trading desk.
Creates recurring, measurable revenue without personal-brand exposure.
risks: Dispatch harms customer operations or equipment.
Cyber intrusion or telemetry failure creates liability.
The licensed partner captures the economics or customer.

structure.control_point: Term-limited device dispatch permissions, secure integrations and site-specific response models obtained through installer channels
structure.critical_dependency: Licensed market-access partner, equipment interoperability, cyber security and enough dependable flexible capacity

thesis: Use installer agreements to contract dispatch permission over compatible SME batteries, HVAC, refrigeration and other flexible loads, then pool them through a licensed balancing or energy-market partner. Sites receive a transparent revenue share; exclusive control rights and measured response histories create an aggregation moat.
title: Installer-Distributed Flexibility Revenue Cooperative
uncertainties: Installer and customer willingness to grant control rights
